comparison: Both evaluate claims C10-C18 about NRL-RBP interactions from GST pull-down experiments. OpenEval finds the evidence well-supported with appropriate controls and statistical significance. Peer reviewers (R3) find the evidence UNCERTAIN, explicitly critiquing incomplete data reporting and stating they 'cannot assess the enrichment of interactions or specificity of interactions with RNA binding proteins based on the reported results.'

Both evaluate claims C36-C43 about NRL binding to DHX9 promoter using ChIP-Seq and EMSA data. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers acknowledge the use of 'state-of-the-art techniques' and treat the genomic binding data as reliable without challenge.

Both evaluate claims C44-C52 about nuclease treatment effects on NRL-DHX9 interactions. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer 3 explicitly accepts the 'specific assays to understand the influence of RNA and R-loops on protein-protein interactions.'

Both evaluate claims C73-C74 about histone modification associations with R-loops. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept the integration of ChIP-Seq datasets with R-loop data without challenge.

OpenEval evaluates C55-C60 (RNase H1 overexpression effects on NRL-DHX9 PLA) as SUPPORTED. Peer R6 evaluates C53-C60 (including DRIP experiments) as SUPPORTED, noting 'adequate evidence of interaction between R-loops and NRL TF' but cautioning the interaction 'can be mediated via multiple R-loop or RNA-binding proteins.'

OpenEval evaluates C70-C72 (GO enrichment at neuronal/synaptic genes) as SUPPORTED. Peer R8 evaluates C70-C72 plus C114 as SUPPORTED, with reviewer 2 explicitly affirming 'R-loops are enriched in genes encoding neuronal function factors.'
Both evaluate C21 (50% overlap with R-loop proteins, Fisher's exact test p=2E-13). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED with strong statistical support that is not questioned by reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates C22-C29 (PLA data in mouse retina) as SUPPORTED. Peer R3 evaluates C24-C35 (PLA data in both mouse and human retina) as SUPPORTED. Editor states findings are 'convincing to support an interaction between NRL and the DHX9 helicase,' and reviewer 3 notes 'multiple orthogonal techniques' validate the interactions.

OpenEval evaluates C30-C35 (PLA in human retina) as SUPPORTED. Peer R3 evaluates C24-C35 (PLA in both mouse and human) as SUPPORTED, with explicit affirmation from all reviewers about the interaction evidence.

OpenEval evaluates C63-C65, C109-C111 (ssDRIP-Seq technical quality and R-loop classification) as SUPPORTED. Peer R7 evaluates C61-C69, C109-C111 (including developmental changes and genomic distributions) as SUPPORTED. Reviewer 2 calls it 'a very interesting study providing genome-wide mapping of R-loops in mammalian retina.'

OpenEval evaluates C66-C69 (genomic distributions of stranded vs unstranded R-loops) as SUPPORTED. Peer R7 includes these claims (C66-C69) within a broader SUPPORTED evaluation of R-loop mapping findings.

OpenEval evaluates C75-C78 (NRL enrichment at R-loops via ChIP-Seq integration) as SUPPORTED. Peer R10 evaluates C75-C80, C112-C113 as UNCERTAIN, noting the interaction 'can be mediated via multiple R-loop or RNA-binding proteins' and emphasizing 'lack of experiments testing the functional significance.'

OpenEval evaluates C79-C80 (gene length associations with R-loops) as SUPPORTED. Peer R10 includes these claims in an UNCERTAIN evaluation, questioning whether NRL directly binds R-loops and noting lack of functional experiments.

OpenEval evaluates C112-C114 (summary of R-loop findings) as SUPPORTED. Peer R10 includes C112-C113 in an UNCERTAIN evaluation focused on whether the NRL-R-loop association is direct or mediated by other proteins.
OpenEval evaluates C112-C114 as SUPPORTED. Peer R8 evaluates C70-C72, C114 as SUPPORTED, with reviewer 2 affirming the gene length findings 'support previous findings from studies in neuronal cells.'

OpenEval evaluates C53-C54 (DRIP experiments showing DHX9 but not DDX5 enrichment in R-loops) as SUPPORTED. Peer R6 evaluates C53-C60 (DRIP plus RNase H1 experiments) as SUPPORTED with adequate evidence.

OpenEval evaluates C61-C62 (developmental R-loop changes and increase in Nrl KO) as SUPPORTED with statistical significance. Peer R7 includes these claims in a broader SUPPORTED evaluation of R-loop mapping studies.

Both evaluate C106-C107 (hypotheses about NRL-RBP interactions in photoreceptor development and disease). Both find these UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes they are 'explicitly stated as hypotheses' requiring experimental validation. Peer reviewers note 'lack of experiments testing the functional significance' and suggest functional experiments would enhance significance.
OpenEval evaluates C1-C7 (background on NRL's role in retinal biology) as SUPPORTED by citations to prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates C8-C9 (background on transcription factors interacting with RNA-binding proteins) as SUPPORTED by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval evaluates C81-C85 (background on R-loop functions) as SUPPORTED by citations to prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates C86-C92 (discussion/interpretation about R-loop regulation and heterochromatin) as SUPPORTED, noting some claims are explicitly speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates C93-C100 (integration of findings about NRL at gene body R-loops and interaction strengths) as SUPPORTED, with some functional interpretations noted as speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates C101-C104 (background on R-loops in neurodegeneration and retinal disease) as SUPPORTED by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
